evidence_excerpts: Three possibilities to consider: if [p] is (fully) grounded in D, then it’s metaphysically necessary that (i) if ∧D then [p] is grounded in D; (ii) if ∧D then something or other is grounded in D; or (iii) if ∧D then p.
text: The relevant sense in which grounding is necessary is the third-style modal consequence that the grounds entail the grounded proposition, not that the grounding relation itself recurs whenever the grounds obtain.
